correction: Verify spelling and punctuation, focusing on comma placement.
Check subject-verb agreement in all clauses and phrases.
Ensure tense consistency throughout the text, confirming no unintended shifts.
Compare each sentence with the original and assess whether awkward or broken sentences were rewritten for clarity and fluency.
Check that the corrections did not introduce new grammatical or structural errors.
Assign a score (1-5) based on how many of the original's errors were fixed and how few remain.
preservation: Compare the original and corrected texts side by side to identify all changes.
Check that nothing was added that was not in the original and that no content was removed or omitted.
Ensure that changes in wording or structure do not alter the original meaning or intent.
Verify that sentences that were already correct and well-structured were left unaltered.
Verify that names, invented words and Japanese honorifics match the original exactly, and that paragraph breaks and formatting are unchanged.
Check that the author's voice, tone and register (formality, narrative perspective) are kept.
Assign a score (1-5) based on how much of the original content, voice and form was kept beyond the needed corrections.
